sanskrit: adyāhave yasya na tulyam anyaṃ; madhyemanuṣyaṃ dhanur ādadānam sarvām imāṃ yaḥ pṛthivīṃ saheta; tathā vidvān yotsyamāno 'smi tena
english: This very day in battle I shall fight, and fully knowing it, against that man who, when he takes up his bow among mortals, has no equal — one who could withstand this whole earth.

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvabhūtāni sadevakāni; prasthe 'jayat khāṇḍave savyasācī ko jīvitaṃ rakṣamāṇo hi tena; yuyutsate mām ṛte mānuṣo 'nyaḥ
english: He, Savyasācin, who upon the plain of Khāṇḍava conquered all beings, the gods among them — what man other than me, caring for his own life, would dare to do battle with him?

sanskrit: ahaṃ tasya pauruṣaṃ pāṇḍavasya; brūyāṃ hṛṣṭaḥ samitau kṣatriyāṇām kiṃ tvaṃ mūrkhaḥ prabhaṣan mūḍhacetā; mām avocaḥ pauruṣam arjunasya
english: I myself, gladly, in the assembly of the kṣatriyas, would proclaim the valor of that son of Pāṇḍu. Why then, you fool, dull-witted and prating, do you recite to me the prowess of Arjuna?

sanskrit: apriyo yaḥ paruṣo niṣṭhuro hi; kṣudraḥ kṣeptā kṣamiṇaś cākṣamāvān hanyām ahaṃ tādṛśānāṃ śatāni; kṣamāmi tvāṃ kṣamayā kālayogāt
english: A spiteful man, harsh and cruel, mean, abusive, intolerant of those who endure — of such men I could slay hundreds. Yet you I forbear, out of patience, because the hour demands it.

sanskrit: avocas tvaṃ pāṇḍavārthe 'priyāṇi; pradharṣayan māṃ mūḍhavat pāpakarman mayy ārjave jihmagatir hatas tvaṃ; mitradrohī saptapadaṃ hi mitram
english: You have spoken hateful words for the Pāṇḍavas' sake, assailing me like an idiot, you doer of evil. Crooked in your ways toward me who am upright, you are as good as slain, a betrayer of friendship — for friendship is sealed in seven steps.

sanskrit: kālas tv ayaṃ mṛtyumayo 'tidāruṇo; duryodhano yuddham upāgamad yat tasyārthasiddhim abhikāṅkṣamāṇas; tam abhyeṣye yatra naikāntyam asti
english: But this is the hour, fraught with death and most terrible, in which Duryodhana has come to war. Longing for the fulfillment of his cause, I shall go to him there, where no withdrawal is possible.

sanskrit: mitraṃ mider nandateḥ prīyater vā; saṃtrāyater mānada modater vā bravīti tac cāmuta viprapūrvāt; tac cāpi sarvaṃ mama duryodhane 'sti
english: A friend, O giver of honor, derives from "to love," "to delight," "to cherish," "to protect," or "to gladden," and so the learned declare from the scriptures of old — and all of that is mine in Duryodhana.

sanskrit: śatruḥ śadeḥ śāsateḥ śāyater vā; śṛṇāter vā śvayater vāpi sarge upasargād bahudhā sūdateś ca; prāyeṇa sarvaṃ tvayi tac ca mahyam
english: A foe derives from "to fell," "to chastise," "to lay low," "to wound," or "to swell," and, with a prefix, in many ways from "to destroy" — and nearly all of that is in you, both for you toward me and for me toward you.

sanskrit: duryodhanārthaṃ tava cāpriyārthaṃ; yaśortham ātmārtham apīśvarārtham tasmād ahaṃ pāṇḍavavāsudevau; yotsye yatnāt karma tat paśya me 'dya
english: For Duryodhana's sake, and to spite you, for glory's sake, for my own sake, and for the lord's sake — therefore I shall fight, with all my strength, against the Pāṇḍava and Vāsudeva. Behold that deed of mine this day.

sanskrit: astrāṇi paśyādya mamottamāni; brāhmāṇi divyāny atha mānuṣāṇi āsādayiṣyāmy aham ugravīryaṃ; dvipottamaṃ mattam ivābhimattaḥ
english: Behold this day my surpassing weapons — sprung from Brahmā, divine, and human alike. I shall close with that man of fierce might as a maddened elephant closes with the lordliest of bulls in rut.

sanskrit: astraṃ brāhmaṃ manasā tad dhy ajayyaṃ; kṣepsye pārthāyāpratimaṃ jayāya tenāpi me naiva mucyeta yuddhe; na cet pated viṣame me 'dya cakram
english: The weapon sprung from Brahmā, unconquerable, peerless, I shall hurl by force of mind against Pārtha for victory; and from it too he shall not escape in battle — unless this day my chariot wheel should sink into broken ground.

sanskrit: vaivasvatād daṇḍahastād varuṇād vāpi pāśinaḥ sagadād vā dhanapateḥ savajrād vāpi vāsavāt
english: Not from the son of Vivasvat with his rod in hand, nor from Varuṇa with his noose, nor from the lord of wealth with his mace, nor even from Vāsava with his thunderbolt —

sanskrit: nānyasmād api kasmāc cid bibhimo hy ātatāyinaḥ iti śalya vijānīhi yathā nāhaṃ bibhemy abhīḥ
english: nor from any other assailant whatsoever do I feel fear. Know this, O Śalya, that I, being fearless, feel no dread.

sanskrit: tasmād bhayaṃ na me pārthān nāpi caiva janārdanāt adya yuddhaṃ hi tābhyāṃ me saṃparāye bhaviṣyati
english: Therefore I have no fear of Pārtha, nor of Janārdana. This day, in the decisive clash, my battle with the two of them shall come to pass.

sanskrit: śvabhre te patatāṃ cakram iti me brāhmaṇo 'vadat yudhyamānasya saṃgrāme prāptasyaikāyane bhayam
english: "Let your wheel sink into a hole" — so a brāhmaṇa once cursed me: that while I fight in battle, brought to a single, narrow pass, peril should fall upon me.

sanskrit: tasmād bibhemi balavad brāhmaṇavyāhṛtād aham ete hi somarājāna īśvarāḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
english: For that reason I dread, and dread greatly, the utterance of the brāhmaṇa — for these moon-pale kings are masters of pleasure and of pain alike.

sanskrit: homadhenvā vatsam asya pramatta iṣuṇāhanam carantam ajane śalya brāhmaṇāt tapaso nidheḥ
english: For heedlessly, O Śalya, I slew with an arrow the calf of his sacred milk-cow as it grazed in a lonely place — the calf of a brāhmaṇa who was a treasury of penance.

sanskrit: īṣādantān saptaśatān dāsīdāsaśatāni ca dadato dvijamukhyāya prasādaṃ na cakāra me
english: Seven hundred elephants with tusks like chariot-poles, and hundreds of bondwomen and bondmen I offered to that foremost of the twice-born, yet he would show me no favor.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇānāṃ śvetavatsānāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa āharan na labhe tasmāt prasādaṃ dvijasattamāt
english: Fourteen thousand black cows with white calves I brought as gifts, yet from that best of the twice-born I won no grace.

sanskrit: ṛddhaṃ gehaṃ sarvakāmair yac ca me vasu kiṃ cana tat sarvam asmai satkṛtya prayacchāmi na cecchati
english: My house, abounding in all desirable things, and whatever wealth was mine — all of that, with honor, I offered to give him, yet he would not have it.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn māṃ yācantam aparāddhaṃ prayatnataḥ vyāhṛtaṃ yan mayā sūta tat tathā na tad anyathā
english: Then he said to me, who, though at fault, entreated him with all my effort: "What I have spoken, O sūta, stands thus; it cannot be otherwise."

sanskrit: anṛtoktaṃ prajā hanyāt tataḥ pāpam avāpnuyāt tasmād dharmābhirakṣārthaṃ nānṛtaṃ vaktum utsahe
english: "A falsehood spoken would destroy my offspring, and from it I should incur sin. Therefore, to safeguard righteousness, I cannot bring myself to utter an untruth."

sanskrit: mā tvaṃ brahmagatiṃ hiṃsyāḥ prāyaścittaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā madvākyaṃ nānṛtaṃ loke kaś cit kuryāt samāpnuhi
english: "Do not seek to thwart the brāhmaṇa's decree; the atonement you have offered has been made. Let no one in the world render my word false — undergo it to the end."

sanskrit: ity etat te mayā proktaṃ kṣiptenāpi suhṛttayā jānāmi tvādhikṣipantaṃ joṣam āssvottaraṃ śṛṇu
english: This much I have told you, though I was provoked, yet out of friendship. I know you for one who reviles me — be silent now, and hear my answer.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ punar mahārāja madrarājam ariṃdamam abhyabhāṣata rādheyaḥ saṃnivāryottaraṃ vacaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then once more, O great king, the son of Rādhā addressed the king of the Madras, that subduer of foes, checking his reply.

sanskrit: yat tvaṃ nidarśanārthaṃ māṃ śalya jalpitavān asi nāhaṃ śakyas tvayā vācā vibhīṣayitum āhave
english: "Whatever, by way of example, you have prated at me, O Śalya — I cannot be frightened by you with mere words in battle."

sanskrit: yadi māṃ devatāḥ sarvā yodhayeyuḥ savāsavāḥ tathāpi me bhayaṃ na syāt kim u pārthāt sakeśavāt
english: "Even if all the gods, with Vāsava at their head, should give me battle, even then I would feel no fear — how much less from Pārtha, though Keśava be at his side."

sanskrit: nāhaṃ bhīṣayituṃ śakyo vāṅmātreṇa kathaṃ cana anyaṃ jānīhi yaḥ śakyas tvayā bhīṣayituṃ raṇe
english: "I cannot in any way be frightened by mere words. Find some other man whom you are able to frighten in battle."

sanskrit: nīcasya balam etāvat pāruṣyaṃ yat tvam āttha mām aśakto 'smadguṇān prāptuṃ valgase bahu durmate
english: "This much only is a low man's strength — the abuse you fling at me. Unable to attain to my qualities, you bluster much, O evil-minded one."

sanskrit: na hi karṇaḥ samudbhūto bhayārtham iha māriṣa vikramārtham ahaṃ jāto yaśorthaṃ ca tathaiva ca
english: "For Karṇa was not born into this world for fear's sake, good sir. I was born for valor's sake, and likewise for glory's sake."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu me tvam ekāgraḥ śṛṇu madrajanādhipa saṃnidhau dhṛtarāṣṭrasya procyamānaṃ mayā śrutam
english: "But hear this from me with full attention, O lord of the Madra people — what I heard told in the presence of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: deśāṃś ca vividhāṃś citrān pūrvavṛttāṃś ca pārthivān brāhmaṇāḥ kathayantaḥ sma dhṛtarāṣṭram upāsate
english: "Brāhmaṇas, recounting many varied and curious lands and the kings of olden times, used to wait upon Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: tatra vṛddhaḥ purāvṛttāḥ kathāḥ kāś cid dvijottamaḥ bāhlīkadeśaṃ madrāṃś ca kutsayan vākyam abravīt
english: "There an aged and foremost of the twice-born, telling certain tales of bygone days, spoke these words in censure of the Bāhlīka land and of the Madras."

sanskrit: bahiṣkṛtā himavatā gaṅgayā ca tiraskṛtāḥ sarasvatyā yamunayā kurukṣetreṇa cāpi ye
english: "Those who are cast out by the Himavat, and scorned by the Gaṅgā, by the Sarasvatī, the Yamunā, and by Kurukṣetra as well —"

sanskrit: pañcānāṃ sindhuṣaṣṭhānāṃ nadīnāṃ ye 'ntar āśritāḥ tān dharmabāhyān aśucīn bāhlīkān parivarjayet
english: "those who dwell between the five rivers, with the Sindhu for the sixth — those Bāhlīkas, outside the law and impure, one should shun."

sanskrit: govardhano nāma vaṭaḥ subhāṇḍaṃ nāma catvaram etad rājakuladvāram ākumāraḥ smarāmy aham
english: "There is a banyan tree called Govardhana, and a market-square called Subhāṇḍa; this is the gate of the royal house — these I remember from my boyhood."

sanskrit: kāryeṇātyarthagāḍhena bāhlīkeṣūṣitaṃ mayā tata eṣāṃ samācāraḥ saṃvāsād vidito mama
english: "On a matter most pressing I once dwelt among the Bāhlīkas; thus, from living among them, their conduct became known to me."

sanskrit: śākalaṃ nāma nagaram āpagā nāma nimnagā jartikā nāma bāhlīkās teṣāṃ vṛttaṃ suninditam
english: "There is a city named Śākala, a river named Āpagā, and the Bāhlīkas called Jartikā — most contemptible is their way of life."

sanskrit: dhānāgauḍāsave pītvā gomāṃsaṃ laśunaiḥ saha apūpamāṃsavāṭyānām āśinaḥ śīlavarjitāḥ
english: "Having drunk liquor of fried grain and molasses, they eat beef together with garlic; gorging on cakes, meat, and parched grain, they are void of good conduct."

sanskrit: hasanti gānti nṛtyanti strībhir mattā vivāsasaḥ nagarāgāravapreṣu bahir mālyānulepanāḥ
english: "They laugh, sing, and dance with their women, drunken and stripped of clothing, upon the walls and houses of the city, garlanded and anointed without."

sanskrit: mattāvagītair vividhaiḥ kharoṣṭraninadopamaiḥ āhur anyonyam uktāni prabruvāṇā madotkaṭāḥ
english: "With sundry drunken ditties, like the braying of asses and camels, they call out to one another, hurling abuse, frenzied with their intoxication."

sanskrit: hā hate hā hatety eva svāmibhartṛhateti ca ākrośantyaḥ pranṛtyanti mandāḥ parvasv asaṃyatāḥ
english: "'Alas, slain! Alas, slain! Alas, my lord and husband, slain!' — so wailing, the wretched women dance about, unrestrained on the festal days."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kilāvaliptānāṃ nivasan kurujāṅgale kaś cid bāhlīkamukhyānāṃ nātihṛṣṭamanā jagau
english: "It is said that a certain one among the Bāhlīka chieftains, those defiled folk, while dwelling in the Kurujāṅgala, sang thus, his heart far from glad:"

sanskrit: sā nūnaṃ bṛhatī gaurī sūkṣmakambalavāsinī mām anusmaratī śete bāhlīkaṃ kuruvāsinam
english: "'Surely that tall, fair woman, clad in fine wool, lies remembering me, a Bāhlīka now dwelling among the Kurus.'"

sanskrit: śatadrukanadīṃ tīrtvā tāṃ ca ramyām irāvatīm gatvā svadeśaṃ drakṣyāmi sthūlaśaṅkhāḥ śubhāḥ striyaḥ
english: "'When I have crossed the Śatadru river and the lovely Irāvatī, and gone to my own land, I shall behold the fair women with their heavy conch-bangles.'"

sanskrit: manaḥśilojjvalāpāṅgā gauryas trikakudāñjanāḥ kevalājinasaṃvītāḥ kūrdantyaḥ priyadarśanāḥ
english: "'Their eye-corners bright with red arsenic, fair-skinned, anointed with collyrium of Trikakud, wrapped in nothing but deerskin, leaping about, lovely to behold —'"

sanskrit: mṛdaṅgānakaśaṅkhānāṃ mardalānāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ kharoṣṭrāśvataraiś caiva mattā yāsyāmahe sukham
english: "'to the sounds of drums and kettledrums, of conches and tabors, mounted on asses, camels, and mules, drunken, we shall journey at our ease.'"

sanskrit: śamīpīlukarīrāṇāṃ vaneṣu sukhavartmasu apūpān saktupiṇḍīś ca khādanto mathitānvitāḥ
english: "'In the woods of śamī, pīlu, and karīra, along the pleasant roads, eating cakes and balls of barley-meal, washed down with buttermilk —'"

sanskrit: pathiṣu prabalā bhūtvā kadāsamṛdite 'dhvani khalopahāraṃ kurvāṇās tāḍayiṣyāma bhūyasaḥ
english: "'grown strong upon the highways, on the unfrequented road we shall fall to robbery and beat down many a traveler.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ hīneṣu vrātyeṣu bāhlīkeṣu durātmasu kaś cetayāno nivasen muhūrtam api mānavaḥ
english: "Among such base, outcaste, evil-souled Bāhlīkas, what man of any sense would dwell even for a moment?"

sanskrit: īdṛśā brāhmaṇenoktā bāhlīkā moghacāriṇaḥ yeṣāṃ ṣaḍbhāgahartā tvam ubhayoḥ śubhapāpayoḥ
english: "Such did the brāhmaṇa declare the Bāhlīkas to be, men of worthless conduct — and you are taker of a sixth part of both their merit and their sin."

sanskrit: ity uktvā brāhmaṇaḥ sādhur uttaraṃ punar uktavān bāhlīkeṣv avinīteṣu procyamānaṃ nibodhata
english: "Having spoken thus, the worthy brāhmaṇa spoke yet again. Mark now what he told of the ill-bred Bāhlīkas."

sanskrit: tatra sma rākṣasī gāti sadā kṛṣṇacaturdaśīm nagare śākale sphīte āhatya niśi dundubhim
english: "There, in the thriving city of Śākala, a rākṣasī sings ever on the dark fourteenth night, beating her drum in the darkness:"

sanskrit: kadā vā ghoṣikā gāthāḥ punar gāsyanti śākale gavyasya tṛptā māṃsasya pītvā gauḍaṃ mahāsavam
english: "'When shall the songstresses again sing their ballads in Śākala, sated with beef, having drunk the great liquor of molasses,'"

sanskrit: gaurībhiḥ saha nārībhir bṛhatībhiḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ palāṇḍugaṇḍūṣayutān khādante caiḍakān bahūn
english: "'together with fair, tall, well-adorned women, eating their fill of mutton washed down with mouthfuls of onion?'"

sanskrit: vārāhaṃ kaukkuṭaṃ māṃsaṃ gavyaṃ gārdabham auṣṭrakam aiḍaṃ ca ye na khādanti teṣāṃ janma nirarthakam
english: "'They who do not eat the flesh of swine, of fowl, of cattle, of asses, of camels, and of sheep — their birth is in vain.'"

sanskrit: iti gāyanti ye mattāḥ śīdhunā śākalāvataḥ sabālavṛddhāḥ kūrdantas teṣu vṛttaṃ kathaṃ bhavet
english: "So sing the dwellers of Śākala, drunk on rum, leaping about with their children and their elders — what good conduct can there be among such folk?"

sanskrit: iti śalya vijānīhi hanta bhūyo bravīmi te yad anyo 'py uktavān asmān brāhmaṇaḥ kurusaṃsadi
english: "Know this, O Śalya — and come, I shall tell you more besides — what yet another brāhmaṇa told us in the Kuru assembly."

sanskrit: pañca nadyo vahanty etā yatra pīluvanāny api śatadruś ca vipāśā ca tṛtīyerāvatī tathā candrabhāgā vitastā ca sindhuṣaṣṭhā bahir gatāḥ
english: "Where these five rivers flow, where too the pīlu-forests stand — the Śatadru, the Vipāśā, the Irāvatī third, the Candrabhāgā and the Vitastā, with the Sindhu sixth, flowing forth beyond —"

sanskrit: āraṭṭā nāma te deśā naṣṭadharmān na tān vrajet vrātyānāṃ dāsamīyānāṃ videhānām ayajvanām
english: "those lands are called Āraṭṭa, lost to righteousness; let none go to them — to the outcastes, the slave-born, the Videhas who keep no sacrifice."

sanskrit: na devāḥ pratigṛhṇanti pitaro brāhmaṇās tathā teṣāṃ pranaṣṭadharmāṇāṃ bāhlīkānām iti śrutiḥ
english: "Neither the gods, nor the fathers, nor the brāhmaṇas accept the offerings of those Bāhlīkas whose law has utterly perished — so runs the sacred tradition."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇena tathā proktaṃ viduṣā sādhusaṃsadi kāṣṭhakuṇḍeṣu bāhlīkā mṛṇmayeṣu ca bhuñjate saktuvāṭyāvalipteṣu śvādilīḍheṣu nirghṛṇāḥ
english: "Thus too declared a learned brāhmaṇa in the assembly of the good: the Bāhlīkas eat, shameless, from wooden and earthen bowls smeared with barley-gruel and licked by dogs and the like."

sanskrit: āvikaṃ cauṣṭrikaṃ caiva kṣīraṃ gārdabham eva ca tadvikārāṃś ca bāhlīkāḥ khādanti ca pibanti ca
english: "The milk of ewes, of camels, and of asses, and whatever is made therefrom, the Bāhlīkas both eat and drink."

sanskrit: putrasaṃkariṇo jālmāḥ sarvānnakṣīrabhojanāḥ āraṭṭā nāma bāhlīkā varjanīyā vipaścitā
english: "Mixing their offspring, base wretches, devouring every kind of food and milk — the Bāhlīkas called Āraṭṭa are to be shunned by the wise."

sanskrit: uta śalya vijānīhi hanta bhūyo bravīmi te yad anyo 'py uktavān sabhyo brāhmaṇaḥ kurusaṃsadi
english: "Mark too, O Śalya — and come, I shall tell you yet more — what still another honorable brāhmaṇa declared in the Kuru assembly."

sanskrit: yugaṃdhare payaḥ pītvā proṣya cāpy acyutasthale tadvad bhūtilaye snātvā kathaṃ svargaṃ gamiṣyati
english: "Having drunk milk in Yugaṃdhara, and lodged in Acyutasthala, and bathed likewise in Bhūtilaya — how shall a man go to heaven?"

sanskrit: pañca nadyo vahanty etā yatra niḥsṛtya parvatāt āraṭṭā nāma bāhlīkā na teṣv āryo dvyahaṃ vaset
english: "Where these five rivers flow, having issued from the mountains — there are the Bāhlīkas called Āraṭṭa; among them no Ārya should dwell two days together."

sanskrit: bahiś ca nāma hlīkaś ca vipāśāyāṃ piśācakau tayor apatyaṃ bāhlīkā naiṣā sṛṣṭiḥ prajāpateḥ
english: "Two piśācas there were, named Bahi and Hlīka, dwelling by the Vipāśā; the Bāhlīkas are their offspring — they are no creation of Prajāpati."

sanskrit: kāraskarān mahiṣakān kaliṅgān kīkaṭāṭavīn karkoṭakān vīrakāṃś ca durdharmāṃś ca vivarjayet
english: "The Kāraskaras, the Māhiṣakas, the Kaliṅgas, the forest Kīkaṭas, the Karkoṭakas and Vīrakas, and the men of evil law — these one should avoid."

sanskrit: iti tīrthānusartāraṃ rākṣasī kā cid abravīt ekarātrā śamīgehe maholūkhalamekhalā
english: "So a certain rākṣasī, dwelling a single night in a house of śamī wood, girt with a great mortar, spoke to a wanderer among the holy fords."

sanskrit: āraṭṭā nāma te deśā bāhlīkā nāma te janāḥ vasātisindhusauvīrā iti prāyo vikutsitāḥ
english: "Those lands are called Āraṭṭa, those people are called Bāhlīka; the Vasātis, the Sindhus, and the Sauvīras — these for the most part stand condemned."

sanskrit: uta śalya vijānīhi hanta bhūyo bravīmi te ucyamānaṃ mayā samyak tad ekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu
english: "Mark too, O Śalya — and come, I shall tell you more — hear with single-minded attention what I now duly relate."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ śilpino geham abhyagacchat purātithiḥ ācāraṃ tatra saṃprekṣya prītaḥ śilpinam abravīt
english: "A brāhmaṇa once came as a guest to the house of an artisan; observing the customs there, well pleased, he said to the craftsman:"

sanskrit: mayā himavataḥ śṛṅgam ekenādhyuṣitaṃ ciram dṛṣṭāś ca bahavo deśā nānādharmasamākulāḥ
english: "'Long have I dwelt alone upon a peak of the Himavat, and I have seen many lands, thronged with diverse customs.'"

sanskrit: na ca kena ca dharmeṇa virudhyante prajā imāḥ sarve hi te 'bruvan dharmaṃ yathoktaṃ vedapāragaiḥ
english: "'And nowhere do these peoples set themselves against righteousness; all of them spoke the law as it is declared by those who have mastered the Vedas —'"

sanskrit: aṭatā tu sadā deśān nānādharmasamākulān āgacchatā mahārāja bāhlīkeṣu niśāmitam
english: "'but ever wandering among lands thronged with diverse customs, O great king, when I came among the Bāhlīkas, this is what I observed:'"

sanskrit: tatraiva brāhmaṇo bhūtvā tato bhavati kṣatriyaḥ vaiśyaḥ śūdraś ca bāhlīkas tato bhavati nāpitaḥ
english: "'There a man, having first been a brāhmaṇa, becomes thereafter a kṣatriya, then a vaiśya, then a śūdra; and the Bāhlīka becomes thereafter a barber —'"

sanskrit: nāpitaś ca tato bhūtvā punar bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ dvijo bhūtvā ca tatraiva punar dāso 'pi jāyate
english: "'and, having become a barber, he becomes a brāhmaṇa once more; and there a man, having been twice-born, is born again even as a slave.'"

sanskrit: bhavaty ekaḥ kule vipraḥ śiṣṭānye kāmacāriṇaḥ gāndhārā madrakāś caiva bāhlīkāḥ ke 'py acetasaḥ
english: "'One man in a family becomes a brāhmaṇa, while the rest do as they please. The Gāndhāras, the Madrakas, and the Bāhlīkas are men devoid of all sense.'"

sanskrit: etan mayā śrutaṃ tatra dharmasaṃkarakārakam kṛtsnām aṭitvā pṛthivīṃ bāhlīkeṣu viparyayaḥ
english: "'This confounding of all law I heard told there; and having wandered the whole earth over, it is among the Bāhlīkas that I found this perversion.'"
